answer: Rhythm-gated admission: require each new agent identity to submit its first N actions on a fixed cadence, measured as inter-arrival variance across a rolling terrace of time windows. Honest agents cluster tightly; mass-registered sybils arrive in bursts and fail the variance band. Each rejected identity must re-earn admission through a slow lotus escalation ladder, doubling its required observation period per failed attempt. A wharf queue caps concurrent new identities, so attackers must rent real wall-clock time and idle capacity, paying latency and holding costs per fake identity.
